newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia urges "strong" Western action in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Croatia urges "strong" Western action in Albania.

text.p: Croatia called on Thursday for "strong and clear" Western action in Albania and said it was pulling some of its diplomatic staff out of Tirana, Croatian state radio reported.

The Croatian Foreign Ministry had decided to evacuate some embassy staff and their families from Tirana and advised Croatian citizens not to travel to Albania because of the high security risk, the radio said.
The ministry called for "strong and clear" action by the international community, including the European Union, and "restrained conduct" on part of Albania's neighbours.
At the same time, the Croatian state-owned oil company INA said it was closing down its operations in Albania.

INA's research operations, carried out 23 km (15 miles) south of Tirana, were interrupted and measures taken to protect the company's property and the oil well, said the radio, quoting the INA press service.
Most of INA's 60 or so experts there would be urgently evacuated, leaving only essential maintenance personnel. No other details were given.
